pages.text:
Arista Networks (ANET) Prospects and Earnings: Revenue Outlook Raised for the Third Time This Year, Non-Cancellable Purchase Commitments Up 2.7x to $9.7 Billion in One Year, and Cost of Goods Sold Awaiting Customer Acceptance Up 5.6x in 18 Months
Hello, this is Umaki.
The stock price of Arista Networks (ticker: ANET) is $210.88 as of the time of writing (closing price on October 12 in the US). It is 43% higher than a year ago, and has risen about 1.8 times in just over half a year from this year's low of $116.13 on March 30. On October 9, it hit a record high of $216.74 at closing.
What has been driving the stock price up is the company's own outlook. The revenue forecast for 2026 has been raised three times this year: from the approximately $10.5 billion presented at last autumn's analyst meeting, to $11.25 billion in February, $11.5 billion in May, and $12.6 billion in August. This represents a projected 40% increase in revenue year-over-year.
On the other hand, other types of figures are appearing in the financial statements. Non-cancellable purchase commitments for components and products increased to $9.7 billion at the end of June, 2.7 times higher than a year ago. The cost of goods sold for products that have been shipped but have not yet been recognized as revenue because customer acceptance (confirmation of receipt) has not been completed has increased 5.6 times in a year and a half.Despite having $13.3 billion in cash on hand, there were zero share buybacks since the beginning of 2026.
Exactly one year ago, on October 13, 2025, Meta, considered one of the largest customers, announced it would adopt NVIDIA's Ethernet switch (Spectrum-X), and Arista's stock price fell by 10% over the two days of the announcement and the following day. As the main players in AI capital expenditure expand, the question of how long the network winner can continue to win remains unanswered.
In this article, I will use primary sources such as the Annual Report (10-K), Quarterly Report (10-Q), earnings call transcripts, and Form 4 (insider trading reports) to examine Arista Networks' earnings and future prospects, including the assumptions currently priced into the stock.
Additionally, on my website, I provide super-analysis of earnings (evaluating earnings on a 100-point scale based on Umaki's assessment) and in-depth information on cryptocurrencies. I would be happy if you could take a look!
👉Click here for the [Umaki's Stocks and Altcoins] blog!
👇 The following article details how to discover ten-baggers. I would appreciate it if you could use that as a reference as well.
The current state of the company supporting AI networks and its stock price
First, let's confirm where the current stock price stands. The stock price and one-year volatility are based on Google Finance chart values, and the company figures are aligned with the earnings materials for the April-June 2026 quarter released on August 4 and the quarterly report filed on August 5.
Stock Price $210.88 (1Y +43.02%) / Market Cap approx. $266 billion / P/E Ratio approx. 67x (trailing 12 months, GAAP) / P/B Ratio approx. 18x / Dividend Yield — (No dividend)
The market capitalization is calculated by multiplying the approximately 1.2612 billion outstanding shares by the stock price. The trailing P/E ratio of 67x is the figure divided by the earnings per share of $3.17 for the past 12 months under standard accounting (GAAP). The adjusted earnings per share for 2027 projected by analysts is $5.22, and when divided by this, the P/E ratio becomes approximately 40x.
Looking at the chart from the left, after hitting a high in the $160 range at the end of October 2025, the stock fell 8.6% the day after the July-September quarterly earnings in November, and treaded water around $130 during the winter. It sank to $116 on March 30, and from there, it recovered more than 50% in just over three weeks until April 22.
In the May earnings for the January-March quarter, despite raising the outlook, the stock fell 13.6% the next day. This was because investors disliked CEO Ullal's comments that component shortages would continue across the industry and pressure profit margins. Since significantly raising the outlook in the August earnings for the April-June quarter, it has risen almost steadily, hitting a record high in October.
5-Year Volatility +765.68% (+$186.52) / All-time High $216.74 (Closing price on October 9, 2026) / Recent Major Decline $129.82 → $64.37 (January 22, 2025 → April 4, 2025, approx. 50% drop)
Arista was founded in 2004 by Andy Bechtolsheim, a co-founder of Sun Microsystems and known as one of Google's first investors, and others. Jayshree Ullal became CEO in 2008, and the company was listed on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2014. Since then, it has split its shares 4-for-1 in 2021 and 2024.
The stock price has increased about 8.7 times in five years, but the journey has not been smooth. In 2025, the stock price halved in about three months, from its high in January to its low in April. This was a period when anxiety about a potential slowdown in AI capital expenditure spread rapidly, fueled by reports of DeepSeek in China releasing a low-cost AI model and the announcement of US tariffs in April.
Since then, in a year and a half, the stock price has reached 3.3 times its low. Mr. Bechtolsheim remains the largest shareholder with 14.6% of the outstanding shares, and Ms. Ullal serves as both Chair and CEO. Kenneth Duda, one of the founding members, serves as President and CTO, and the faces at the center of the technology have not changed much since the founding period.
The mechanism for earning through switches and EOS
Arista's core product is the Ethernet switch that connects servers within data centers. In AI training and inference, tens to hundreds of thousands of GPUs exchange data without rest, so the speed and stability of the network connecting them determine GPU utilization rates.
The semiconductors at the heart of the products are not made in-house but are mainly purchased from Broadcom. What sets them apart is EOS, a network OS that runs as the same single software across all products. Product assembly is entrusted to contract manufacturers such as Jabil, Sanmina, and Foxconn, with production taking place in Malaysia, Vietnam, Mexico, and other locations.
According to the company's explanation, the breakdown of revenue for 2025 was as follows.
By customer type: 48% from large cloud and AI giants, 32% from general enterprises and financial institutions, and 20% from AI-specialized and other cloud operators.
By product: 65% from core products for data centers and AI, 18% from office networks (campus) and wide-area routing, and 17% from software and services.
There are two customers that account for more than 10% of revenue, and in 2025, they accounted for 26% and 16% of revenue, respectively. 42% from just two companies in total. Although the company does not disclose the names, CEO Ullal mentioned Microsoft and Meta as their oldest partners during the earnings call, and they are believed to be these two companies.
The company had approximately 5,115 employees at the end of 2025. The adjusted operating margin for the April-June quarter was 49.9%, meaning nearly half of the revenue remains as operating profit. I believe that a company that buys semiconductors and puts them in boxes is able to achieve profit margins close to those of a software company because of EOS and its long-standing relationships with customers.
💡 Arista is a company that has earned its success through software and customer relationships without owning its own semiconductors. Because its strengths are clear, it is worth keeping in mind from the start its dependence on two large customers and Broadcom, which are parties it cannot control itself.
Earnings details: Guidance raised three times, gross margin declined
From here, we will look at the earnings for the April-June quarter released on August 4. While revenue growth is strong as the headline suggests, there are figures that should be read with caution when breaking down profit margins and revenue sources step by step.
Revenue up 37.7%, full-year guidance to $12.6 billion
Revenue for the April-June quarter was $3.0357 billion, up 37.7% year-on-year and up 12.1% from the previous quarter. This exceeded the approximately $2.8 billion guidance the company issued in May by more than $230 million. Quarterly revenue exceeded $3 billion for the first time, and CEO Ullal reflected that five years ago in 2021, annual revenue was $2.9 billion.
Product revenue was $2.6052 billion (+38.8%), and service revenue from maintenance and software was $430.5 million (+31.3%). GAAP net income was $1.2129 billion, or $0.95 per share. Adjusted earnings per share, excluding stock-based compensation, was $1.02, a 40% increase from $0.73 in the same period last year.
The revenue guidance for 2026 has been raised as follows.
Analyst meeting in autumn 2025: approximately $10.5 billion
February 2026 (October-December quarter earnings): approximately $11.25 billion (25% increase)
May 2026 (January-March quarter earnings): approximately $11.5 billion
August 2026 (April-June quarter earnings): Approximately $12.6 billion (40% increase)
The guidance for the July-September quarter is approximately $3.3 billion in revenue, with adjusted earnings per share of $1.06 to $1.08. Since revenue for the first half was $5.7447 billion, calculating backward from the full-year $12.6 billion, it implies revenue of approximately $3.55 billion for the October-December quarter. Revenue for the second half is about 1.19 times that of the first half, structured so that it can be achieved even without the significant upside seen in the first half.
CEO Ullal stated during the earnings call that all figures, including AI and campus, are trending upward. Furthermore, the guidance is based on the extent to which components can be secured, and there is room for further upside if supply eases. What determines this company's revenue right now is the supply side rather than demand.
While revenue grew by nearly 40%, the gross margin has declined. The GAAP gross margin for the April-June quarter was 62.9%, down 2.3 percentage points from 65.2% in the same period last year. The company cites the increased proportion of sales to large customers with significant discounts as the primary reason.
Another burden is the rising cost of components such as memory. During the February earnings call, CEO Ullal candidly stated that the memory situation had deteriorated significantly, that they had no choice but to accept almost any price to secure supply, and that the pricing was terrible. Although the gross margin for the April-June quarter rose by 1 percentage point from the previous quarter, 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points of this was a temporary boost from tariff refunds.
The company has maintained its 2026 gross margin guidance at 62-64%. Regarding price increases, the explanation was that since they are currently fulfilling backlogs, the impact will be felt toward the end of the year or next year. Costs rise first, and price increases take effect later—following this sequence, they expect downward pressure on the gross margin for some time.
As for the operating margin, revenue growth outpaced expense growth, and the adjusted guidance for 2026 was raised to 48-49%. However, the long-term model for 2026-2029 presented by the company in the fall of 2025 was a gross margin of 60-64% and an operating margin of 43-45%. Current profit margins are higher than the company's own long-term assumptions.
Deferred revenue up 2.5x in a year and a half
The most difficult figure to interpret in Arista's earnings is deferred revenue (the amount for which payment has been received or billed to customers but has not yet been recognized as revenue). Is Open AI Rack Launch Altering The Investment Case For Arista Networks Stock?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 5:10 AM CDT 6 min read
Arista Networks recently launched an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, including the Etherlink SU-144 architecture, to support high-density AI infrastructure with up to 144 accelerators per rack and liquid-cooled designs tailored for extreme power and thermal demands.
The ESUN-based platforms and Netdi foundation aim to give cloud and AI operators an open, standards-focused alternative to proprietary interconnects, linking Arista's hardware closely to neocloud cost-per-token priorities and multi-vendor AI compute ecosystems.
This development also shapes Arista Networks' broader investment narrative, with a focus on the Etherlink SU-144 AI rack-scale expansion.
Spot opportunities around Arista Networks' AI buildout by scanning a hand-picked set of 55 AI infrastructure stocks.
Arista Networks Investment Narrative Recap
To own Arista Networks, you need to believe high bandwidth AI and cloud networking keeps expanding and that hyperscalers and neocloud platforms keep leaning into open Ethernet fabrics rather than closing into proprietary islands. The Etherlink SU-144 launch fits that thesis operationally by deepening Arista's role inside dense AI racks, but the recent product news does not change the basic story that execution depends on a few very large buyers.
In the near term, the key catalyst is how management frames AI fabrics demand and 2026 guidance on the upcoming earnings call, especially in the context of recent share price volatility. The biggest risk is that AI buildouts or U.S. data center permitting slow while Arista has already locked in multiyear chip and memory commitments, which could leave utilization and gross margin under pressure.
The Etherlink SU-144 scale up architecture is the announcement that matters most here because it goes straight to the core AI catalyst for Arista Networks. By extending Ethernet into tightly coupled accelerator domains of up to 144 XPUs per rack and over 1,000 XPUs across racks, the firm is trying to stay aligned with the way large customers design AI clusters.
That same launch also highlights the execution swing factors. Liquid cooled, 100 kW plus racks, UEC based fabrics, and support for multiple scale up protocols increase Arista's footprint but require heavy up front commitments and integration work. If hyperscalers moderate AI capital spending or shift toward more in house solutions, this expanded ESUN and Etherlink stack could take longer to absorb than current plans assume.
What the Current Arista Networks Consensus Is Pricing In
Analysts are effectively telling you that Arista Networks has to keep growing into its AI and cloud ambitions for current expectations to hold. The consensus setup assumes revenue expands at about 26.6% a year over the next few years, while profit margins stay steady at 38.4%. That combination keeps the story firmly tied to execution rather than margin repair.
On earnings, the group forecast points to US$8.2b of profit by 2029 versus US$4.0b today. That is roughly a doubling of earnings, or a 2x step up from current levels, and it comes with a wide spread of views between the most optimistic and most cautious analysts. For investors tracking the AI buildout, that range underlines how much uncertainty still sits around long range demand for Ethernet based fabrics, including platforms like Etherlink SU-144.
The same playbook underpins the revenue line. Consensus numbers imply roughly US$21.4b of sales in 2029 if Arista Networks delivers on the AI and campus targets embedded in recent guidance. That profile lines up with the assumption of mid 20s top line expansion and a business that keeps its profitability broadly where it is today rather than swinging to a very different margin structure.
Valuation thinking in the analyst reports also leans heavily on those 2029 profit targets. To make the current price targets add up, Arista Networks would need to trade on a P/E of about 47.8x those projected earnings, compared with roughly 62.2x on today's earnings base and around 34.4x for the wider US communications peer group. The message to you is simple: belief in the AI networking path, including Etherlink and ESUN driven racks, is what is doing most of the work in these models.
Arista Networks' narrative projects US$21.4b revenue and US$8.2b earnings by 2029. This requires 26.6% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$4.2b from US$4.0b today.

One bullish twist you might explore is the idea that Arista Networks could already have more future demand lined up than the baseline narrative assumes. The most optimistic analysts were penciling in about US$25.2b of revenue and US$9.5b of earnings by 2029 before this Etherlink SU-144 news, so their story may become more extreme or be reined in as forecasts refresh.

pages.text:
Networking Stocks Rally as Tech Rebound Lifts AI Gear Makers: Ciena and Arista Climb 4%, but Cisco Barely Moves
AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.

As cloud computing and public safety technology evolve, investors are weighing high-growth infrastructure against defensive software ecosystems. Choosing between Arista Networks (ANET -0.96%) and Axon Enterprise (AXON +2.49%) requires balancing different risk profiles.
Arista provides high-speed networking equipment that powers modern data centers, while Axon dominates the law enforcement technology market through Taser devices and software. Both companies benefit from secular trends in automation and digitization, making them compelling candidates for growth-oriented portfolios looking for market leaders in their respective categories.
Arista Networks is a prominent player among tech stocks that design high-performance networking platforms for large-scale data centers. Its solutions are vital for artificial intelligence workloads that require massive bandwidth and low latency. The company primarily serves cloud titans and specialty providers. In its latest annual report, filed for 2025, customer concentration remained a key factor. Two major end customers accounted for 16% and 26% of revenue, respectively. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business if spending patterns shift.
In 2025, revenue reached $9 billion, representing approximately 29% year-over-year growth. The ongoing build-out of infrastructure for generative artificial intelligence drove this expansion. The company reported net income of roughly $3.5 billion for the period. Its net margin, which measures how much profit is retained from every dollar of sales, was close to 39%.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 3.0x. This metric indicates the company has $3 in current assets for every $1 in short-term liabilities, suggesting strong liquidity. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating the company has no debt relative to shareholders' equity. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was roughly $4.3 billion.
Axon Enterprise specializes in hardware and cloud-based software for public safety agencies. Its ecosystem includes Taser energy devices, body-worn cameras, and digital evidence management systems. Unlike its peer, Axon has a diverse customer base, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of net sales in 2025. The company is increasingly focused on its software-as-a-service offerings, which provide recurring revenue streams from law enforcement and federal agencies.
In 2025, revenue reached close to $2.8 billion, a significant 33.5% increase over the prior year. This growth highlights the increasing adoption of cloud software and next-generation safety devices. However, the company reported net income of approximately $125 million, resulting in a net margin of roughly 4.5%. This lower net margin reflects heavy investments in research and development to stay ahead of technological shifts.
According to its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.6x. This indicates that total debt is 60% of shareholders' equity. The current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to pay short-term debts, is roughly 2.5x.
Free cash flow was approximately $75 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning this non-cash add-back heavily inflates reported cash generation.
Arista Networks faces revenue concentration risk, as a few large cloud and AI customers drive a significant share of its sales. The company also relies heavily on Broadcom for switching chips, making it vulnerable to supply chain disruptions. Competitive pressure from Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Extreme Networks creates persistent pricing pressure. Furthermore, geopolitical tensions and trade controls concerning China affect its global manufacturing operations and costs.
Axon Enterprise is dependent on law enforcement budgets, which can be affected by political shifts or economic constraints. The company also faces persistent risks from product liability and legal claims related to the use of its Taser devices. Rapid technological change requires constant innovation in AI and machine learning, which carries high research costs. Additionally, the company reported a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of Dec. 31, 2025, related to revenue recognition.
Investors must choose between Arista Networks, which trades at a lower Forward P/E, and Axon Enterprise, which has a significantly lower P/S ratio.
Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.
The Forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Arista and Axon are both quality growth stocks to consider for the long term, but Axon is the stock I would buy right now. This is after the stock has fallen over 50% from its 2025 all-time high, providing an attractive entry point to invest in this dominant technology provider for law enforcement.
Arista is consistently posting high-double-digit revenue growth and will likely continue to do so, given the strong tailwinds in AI infrastructure spending. But Axon is posting equally impressive growth, as it pivots to providing AI-powered software. The company reported seeing robust demand last quarter, with 70% year-over-year growth in its software business.
Arista is generating higher margins, but this is largely priced into the stock's valuation. Analysts expect Arista's earnings to grow at an annualized rate of about 18% in the coming years. Its forward P/E of 44 puts the PEG ratio at over 2x.
Axon is expected to deliver 39% annualized earnings growth, with the stock trading at a forward P/E of about 53x, as of Oct. 20, 2026. That's a more attractive PEG multiple of 1.36x.
These are both solid growth stocks, but Axon is potentially the more undervalued, making it the one I would buy now.

Investors looking for the next phase of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure growth may want to look beyond semiconductor sector designers and examine the networking backbone tying the compute together. Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) recently hit an all-time high of about $217, capping a year-to-date climb of around 61%.
This price action reflects a shift in how hyperscalers approach data center architecture. Cloud providers are actively seeking alternatives to single-vendor systems that lock them into specific hardware ecosystems.
By partnering with compute leaders to develop vendor-agnostic network switches, Arista is capturing a growing share of the spending allocated to expand computing power and networking capacity in their data centers.
Forbes calls this a "golden era" for retirement income (Ad)
Forbes recently called a new category of exchange-traded income funds a 'golden era,' and Bloomberg noted the eye-popping yields are fueling a boom among everyday investors. Three years ago, barely a dozen of these funds existed - today there are more than 100, holding over $140 billion.
These funds trade on the NYSE and NASDAQ and are built to generate monthly income. Some investors are targeting $5,000 a month with roughly one-tenth of the nest egg Wall Street says you need.
Watch the short briefing to see how this income approach works
Unlocking the Rack: Ethernet's AI Evolution
The driver behind Arista's recent breakout was the launch of an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio custom-built for high-density networking workloads. Engineered alongside a consortium that includes Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), this hardware rollout targets the physical constraints of modern data centers.
The launch's centerpiece is the Etherlink SU-144, an architecture that connects up to 144 accelerators in a single-hop network. This system can also scale to connect about 1,024 accelerators across multiple racks. By integrating 7060EX7 switches with liquid cooling and next-generation optics, this setup pushes rack capacity to approximately 6.5 petabits per second.
For data center operators, this translates to an estimated 50% reduction in physical footprint. Less space and thermal output let operators pack more computational power into existing facilities. This footprint reduction is critical as artificial intelligence models grow larger and more complex, demanding higher power density per square foot.
Short-Circuiting the InfiniBand Monopoly
For the past few years, proprietary interconnects like NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) InfiniBand have largely dominated AI networking. While highly effective, these closed systems create vendor lock-in, forcing cloud providers to source both compute and networking hardware from the same supplier to ensure compatibility.
The industry is pushing back. Hyperscalers are actively funding and adopting open standards to regain leverage and diversify their supply chains, and Arista is serving as a vehicle for this capital rotation.
By leaning into the Ethernet for Scale-up Networks initiative and the Ultra Ethernet Consortium, Arista offers a standardized alternative that lets cloud operators mix and match hardware from different manufacturers. The Ultra Ethernet Consortium is specifically designed to tune Ethernet protocols for the unique data loads of model training and inference. These tasks were previously thought to require bespoke networking hardware. Meta and Microsoft's involvement in the recent product launch validates that demand for interoperability is coming directly from the world's largest buyers of technology infrastructure.

Ian Cooper's newest strategy targets triple-digit returns in just 9 days. It doesn't work every time, but a 73% win rate and 2,671% return on capital stand on their own.
Ian is breaking down the full strategy and offering his newest report at no charge.

Capturing market share is only half the equation. Converting that share into profitable growth is what justifies multiple expansion. Arista reported revenue of about $3.04 billion in its most recent quarter, up about 37.7% year over year. Earnings per share came in at $1.02, beating consensus estimates and showing the company's ability to scale operations efficiently.
The balance sheet adds another layer of stability. Arista holds about $13.3 billion in cash and cash equivalents and has near-zero debt. This capital structure provides flexibility for research and development without the risks associated with leverage. The firm also generated a return on equity of nearly 31%, indicating efficient use of shareholder capital.
Looking ahead, management raised forward guidance, projecting roughly $3.3 billion in revenue and earnings per share between $1.06 and $1.08 for the upcoming quarter. This guidance signals that data center spending is accelerating rather than plateauing.
Investors evaluating Arista will notice a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of about 67. While that figure appears stretched in isolation, the price-to-earnings growth ratio sits at a defensible 2.53. For an infrastructure provider generating around 38% net margins and nearly 40% top-line growth, this premium multiple aligns with the expanding total addressable market for backend networks.
When a stock trades near all-time highs, insider trading activity often draws scrutiny. Recent filings show that CEO Jayshree Ullal and founder Andreas Bechtolsheim sold portions of their holdings, along with additional selling by directors.
While large distributions can signal a lack of executive conviction, context matters. These sales were executed through pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. Given Arista's unleveraged balance sheet and the fact that these executives still maintain large positions in the stock after the sales, these moves reflect standard portfolio diversification rather than a warning sign.
On the institutional side, capital continues to flow into Arista. Funds like Confluence Investment Management and MassMutual Private Wealth recently accumulated shares, indicating that large asset managers see a sustained runway for the open Ethernet thesis.
Wall Street analysts maintain a consensus moderate Buy rating, with recent price target upgrades reflecting confidence in Arista's execution path. By analyzing institutional fund flows, investors can see a broader consensus forming around the long-term viability of vendor-agnostic infrastructure.
The transition from proprietary compute islands to open, interoperable data centers is a multi-year trend. Arista is dismantling closed networking monopolies by giving hyperscalers what they require: raw bandwidth and hardware flexibility. The partnership with AMD and other technology heavyweights positions Arista to capture a significant wave of infrastructure spending over the coming quarters.
As artificial intelligence models grow more complex, the physical constraints of power, thermal management, and cross-rack communication will only increase. Investors reviewing their technology allocations might consider adding Arista Networks to their watchlists as the rollout of the Etherlink portfolio begins to be reflected in upcoming earnings reports. Those with a longer time horizon could find its debt-free balance sheet and expanding margins a compelling counterbalance to the higher volatility often seen in pure-play semiconductor equities.

Here is What to Know Beyond Why Arista Networks, Inc. (ANET) is a Trending Stock
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 5 min read
Arista Networks (ANET) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.
Over the past month, shares of this cloud networking company have returned -11.2%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.5% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Arista Networks falls in, has gained 0.8%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?
While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.
Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.
Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, Arista Networks is expected to post earnings of $1.08 per share, indicating a change of +44% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.
For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $4.12 points to a change of +38.3% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.
For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.12 indicates a change of +24.3% from what Arista Networks is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.
With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Arista Networks.
The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:
12-month consensus EPS estimate for ANET
Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.
For Arista Networks, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $3.31 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +43.5%. For the current and next fiscal years, $12.63 billion and $16 billion estimates indicate +40.3% and +26.7% changes, respectively.
Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Arista Networks Advances 4% While Ciena Soars 11% on AI Networking Demand; Cisco Rises 3%
Three networking and optical stocks are surging well past the broader market today, but the gaps between their gains reveal something specific about where AI infrastructure demand is hitting a wall.
Published October 6, 2026, 12:56pm ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.

AI networking demand is lifting Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET | ANET Price Prediction), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Ciena (NYSE:CIEN), with shares of the optical supplier pulling far ahead of the two switching vendors. No company announcement accounts for the gain in Arista stock, which sits inside a broader bid across networking and optical equipment. That leaves the relative size of the three moves as the clearest signal of where the market sees demand outrunning supply.
Ciena stock is at $431.18, up 11% in midday trading, the largest gain of the three by a wide margin. Meanwhile, Arista Networks stock is at $214.34, up 4%, the smallest advance in the group. Cisco stock trades at $115.83, up 3%, landing between the other two.
For context, the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 0.63%, a modest gain for the broader tech sector. At the same time, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.76%. Against those benchmarks, shares of Ciena, Arista and Cisco are each running well ahead of both the tech sector and the overall market, a sign that the buying is targeted at network equipment.
Bernstein Note Ties Networking to Optical
On October 1, Bernstein initiated coverage of Arista Networks with an Outperform rating and a price target of $250, arguing that networking and optical suppliers both benefit from AI infrastructure spending, with demand still running ahead of supply. That note is several days old and serves as background to the session. The detail that matters now is the note’s pairing of networking with optical, since shares of Ciena, the optical name in this group, are running hardest.
Arista Networks reported its second-quarter 2026 results in early August, with revenue growth of 37.7% from a year earlier. Demand across AI networking, data centers, campus and routing drove that growth, giving the company several engines working at once, and such breadth underpins Arista’s longer-term story, though the August report isn’t fresh news for the stock and doesn’t explain the latest buying on its own.
Transport Layer Shows Where Scarcity Sits
Inside data centers, Arista and Cisco sell the switches and routers that move traffic, while Ciena supplies the optical transport layer that carries traffic between those facilities. A buildout that adds computing capacity in more locations lifts transport demand before it lifts switching demand. That sequencing is the structural reason Ciena, Arista and Cisco shares don’t move in lockstep, even when the same AI theme is driving all three.
Ciena stock running several times harder than Arista stock points to the transport layer as the place where the market currently sees scarcity. Bernstein’s note collapsed exactly that distinction by grouping networking and optical suppliers together under one spending thesis. Arista stock is the smallest mover of the three, which complicates reading the session as a story about Arista itself.
Between those extremes, Cisco stock is advancing solidly, which suggests the bid extends across the equipment layer as a whole. The middle slot held by Cisco stock also gives the market a useful reference point, since a broad rally lifts the diversified networking giant while the sharpest gains collect in optical transport. Such a pattern fits a market rewarding AI infrastructure broadly. It reserves its biggest premium for the scarcest piece (we profiled seven of these non-chip AI suppliers, from networking to power and cooling, in a free report you can grab here).
Evidence that switching demand is tightening the way transport demand appears to be would tie the next move in Arista stock to the company specifically, and this session doesn’t supply it. Traders could look for signs that Arista faces the same supply pressure Bernstein described across networking and optical suppliers. Until then, Ciena stock remains a clearer expression of the transport scarcity the market is pricing.
Shareholders may want to keep an eye on whether Cisco stock continues advancing alongside Ciena and Arista, since a sustained broad rally would support the view that AI networking spending is lifting every tier of the equipment stack. A fade in CSCO stock while CIEN stock holds its gains would point to a narrower trade concentrated in optical transport. Either outcome may clarify whether the equipment rally has staying power beyond the optical names.
Ciena stock carries the most risk of the three if transport scarcity eases, since it is running so far ahead of the group, while Arista and Cisco shares are riding the same spending wave with smaller swings. Investors weighing their exposure should calibrate their holdings carefully given that a sector-wide bid across networking and optical equipment is driving all three stocks. Keeping their positions in any one of these names moderate limits how much their portfolios lean on a single tier of the AI networking buildout.

Arista Networks (ANET -0.96%) is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 3, but I think the most important numbers in the report won't have anything to do with the third quarter.
Instead, I'll be watching what management says about the final three months of 2026.
According to Yahoo Finance, Wall Street expects the artificial intelligence (AI) networking company to generate $3.6 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and earnings of $1.15 per share. Those are some pretty ambitious targets, but I think Arista has a good chance to exceed them.
And if management delivers guidance that beats those expectations, I think Arista stock could soar after Nov. 3.
Image source: Getty Images.
Arista has become an important supplier of the high-speed networking equipment that connects processors and servers inside massive artificial intelligence data centers.
Companies such as Nvidia are developing increasingly powerful graphics processing units (GPUs), but those chips can't reach their full potential unless enormous amounts of information can move between them quickly.
Arista makes Ethernet switches that help eliminate networking bottlenecks, allowing thousands of processors to work together on demanding AI applications.
The company reported second-quarter revenue of $3.03 billion, a 37.7% increase from a year ago. Diluted earnings per share reached $0.95, compared with $0.70 in the year-earlier period. Management also projected third-quarter revenue of approximately $3.3 billion.
That's in line with what Wall Street projects. According to Yahoo Finance, the consensus Q3 estimates are $3.33 billion in revenue and $1.08 in earnings per share (EPS).
I'm not too worried about Q3 results -- instead, I'd rather look ahead. Investors already know that Arista is growing quickly. What they need to know now is whether demand for their networking equipment will remain strong as cloud computing companies continue to expand their AI infrastructure.
That's why fourth-quarter guidance could be more important than the third-quarter results themselves.

Arista's path to topping Wall Street expectations
Arista has been introducing new networking products designed to handle increasingly demanding AI workloads.
Its 7060XE7 platform supports connections running at 1.6 terabits per second, while its recently announced Etherlink SU-144 architecture can connect up to 144 AI accelerators within a single-hop network.
Those capabilities are becoming more important as AI data centers grow larger and companies look for ways to get more performance from their expensive processors.
The opportunity is substantial, but so is the competition. Nvidia and Cisco Systems are also pursuing the AI networking market, and Arista depends heavily on spending by major cloud computing companies. Still, I think the company's recent growth gives management a reasonable opportunity to surprise Wall Street.
Arista typically provides quarterly revenue and margin guidance rather than an explicit earnings-per-share forecast. So I'll be watching whether its fourth-quarter revenue outlook exceeds $3.6 billion and whether its projected profitability supports earnings above the $1.15 consensus estimate.
A revenue forecast above expectations would suggest that demand for Arista's networking equipment remains stronger than Wall Street anticipated. Healthy margins would make that growth even more valuable to shareholders.

Here's Why Arista Networks (ANET) Could be Great Choice for a Bottom Fisher

Shares of Arista Networks (ANET) have been struggling lately and have lost 12% over the past week. However, a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session, which could mean that the stock found support with bulls being able to counteract the bears. So, it could witness a trend reversal down the road.
While the formation of a hammer pattern is a technical indication of nearing a bottom with potential exhaustion of selling pressure, rising optimism among Wall Street analysts about the future earnings of this cloud networking company is a solid fundamental factor that enhances the prospects of a trend reversal for the stock.
What is a Hammer Chart and How to Trade It?
This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'
In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.
When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.
Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.
Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.
Here's What Makes the Trend Reversal More Likely for ANET
An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that ANET has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.
The consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 0% over the last 30 days. This means that the Wall Street analysts covering ANET are majorly in agreement about the company's potential to report better earnings than what they predicted earlier.
If this is not enough, you should note that ANET currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .
Moreover, a Zacks Rank of 2 for Arista Networks is a more conclusive indication of a potential trend reversal, as the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator that helps investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve.

Arista Networks vs. Axon Enterprise: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 10:16 PM CDT 6 min read
As cloud computing and public safety technology evolve, investors are weighing high-growth infrastructure against defensive software ecosystems. Choosing between Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) and Axon Enterprise (NASDAQ:AXON) requires balancing different risk profiles.
Arista provides high-speed networking equipment that powers modern data centers, while Axon dominates the law enforcement technology market through Taser devices and software. Both companies benefit from secular trends in automation and digitization, making them compelling candidates for growth-oriented portfolios looking for market leaders in their respective categories.
Arista Networks is a prominent player among tech stocks that design high-performance networking platforms for large-scale data centers. Its solutions are vital for artificial intelligence workloads that require massive bandwidth and low latency. The company primarily serves cloud titans and specialty providers. In its latest annual report, filed for 2025, customer concentration remained a key factor. Two major end customers accounted for 16% and 26% of revenue, respectively. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business if spending patterns shift.
In 2025, revenue reached $9 billion, representing approximately 29% year-over-year growth. The ongoing build-out of infrastructure for generative artificial intelligence drove this expansion. The company reported net income of roughly $3.5 billion for the period. Its net margin, which measures how much profit is retained from every dollar of sales, was close to 39%.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 3.0x. This metric indicates the company has $3 in current assets for every $1 in short-term liabilities, suggesting strong liquidity. The debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, indicating the company has no debt relative to shareholders' equity. Free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was roughly $4.3 billion.
Axon Enterprise specializes in hardware and cloud-based software for public safety agencies. Its ecosystem includes Taser energy devices, body-worn cameras, and digital evidence management systems. Unlike its peer, Axon has a diverse customer base, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of net sales in 2025. The company is increasingly focused on its software-as-a-service offerings, which provide recurring revenue streams from law enforcement and federal agencies.
In 2025, revenue reached close to $2.8 billion, a significant 33.5% increase over the prior year. This growth highlights the increasing adoption of cloud software and next-generation safety devices. However, the company reported net income of approximately $125 million, resulting in a net margin of roughly 4.5%. This lower net margin reflects heavy investments in research and development to stay ahead of technological shifts.
According to its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.6x. This indicates that total debt is 60% of shareholders' equity. The current ratio, a measure of a company's ability to pay short-term debts, is roughly 2.5x.
Free cash flow was approximately $75 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning this non-cash add-back heavily inflates reported cash generation.
Arista Networks faces revenue concentration risk, as a few large cloud and AI customers drive a significant share of its sales. The company also relies heavily on Broadcom for switching chips, making it vulnerable to supply chain disruptions. Competitive pressure from Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Extreme Networks creates persistent pricing pressure. Furthermore, geopolitical tensions and trade controls concerning China affect its global manufacturing operations and costs.
Axon Enterprise is dependent on law enforcement budgets, which can be affected by political shifts or economic constraints. The company also faces persistent risks from product liability and legal claims related to the use of its Taser devices. Rapid technological change requires constant innovation in AI and machine learning, which carries high research costs. Additionally, the company reported a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as of Dec. 31, 2025, related to revenue recognition.
Investors must choose between Arista Networks, which trades at a lower Forward P/E, and Axon Enterprise, which has a significantly lower P/S ratio.
Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.
The Forward P/E compares the stock price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.
Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Arista and Axon are both quality growth stocks to consider for the long term, but Axon is the stock I would buy right now. This is after the stock has fallen over 50% from its 2025 all-time high, providing an attractive entry point to invest in this dominant technology provider for law enforcement.
Arista is consistently posting high-double-digit revenue growth and will likely continue to do so, given the strong tailwinds in AI infrastructure spending. But Axon is posting equally impressive growth, as it pivots to providing AI-powered software. The company reported seeing robust demand last quarter, with 70% year-over-year growth in its software business.
Arista is generating higher margins, but this is largely priced into the stock's valuation. Analysts expect Arista's earnings to grow at an annualized rate of about 18% in the coming years. Its forward P/E of 44 puts the PEG ratio at over 2x.
Axon is expected to deliver 39% annualized earnings growth, with the stock trading at a forward P/E of about 53x, as of Oct. 20, 2026. That's a more attractive PEG multiple of 1.36x.
These are both solid growth stocks, but Axon is potentially the more undervalued, making it the one I would buy now.

Hello, this is Umaki.
The stock price of Arista Networks (ticker: ANET) is $210.88 as of the time of writing (closing price on October 12 in the US). It is 43% higher than a year ago, and has risen about 1.8 times in just over half a year from this year's low of $116.13 on March 30. On October 9, it hit a record high of $216.74 at closing.
What has been driving the stock price up is the company's own outlook. The revenue forecast for 2026 has been raised three times this year: from the approximately $10.5 billion presented at last autumn's analyst meeting, to $11.25 billion in February, $11.5 billion in May, and $12.6 billion in August. This represents a projected 40% increase in revenue year-over-year.
On the other hand, other types of figures are appearing in the financial statements. Non-cancellable purchase commitments for components and products increased to $9.7 billion at the end of June, 2.7 times higher than a year ago. The cost of goods sold for products that have been shipped but have not yet been recognized as revenue because customer acceptance (confirmation of receipt) has not been completed has increased 5.6 times in a year and a half.Despite having $13.3 billion in cash on hand, there were zero share buybacks since the beginning of 2026.
Exactly one year ago, on October 13, 2025, Meta, considered one of the largest customers, announced it would adopt NVIDIA's Ethernet switch (Spectrum-X), and Arista's stock price fell by 10% over the two days of the announcement and the following day. As the main players in AI capital expenditure expand, the question of how long the network winner can continue to win remains unanswered.
In this article, I will use primary sources such as the Annual Report (10-K), Quarterly Report (10-Q), earnings call transcripts, and Form 4 (insider trading reports) to examine Arista Networks' earnings and future prospects, including the assumptions currently priced into the stock.
Additionally, on my website, I provide super-analysis of earnings (evaluating earnings on a 100-point scale based on Umaki's assessment) and in-depth information on cryptocurrencies. I would be happy if you could take a look!
👉Click here for the [Umaki's Stocks and Altcoins] blog!
👇 The following article details how to discover ten-baggers. I would appreciate it if you could use that as a reference as well.
The current state of the company supporting AI networks and its stock price
First, let's confirm where the current stock price stands. The stock price and one-year volatility are based on Google Finance chart values, and the company figures are aligned with the earnings materials for the April-June 2026 quarter released on August 4 and the quarterly report filed on August 5.
Stock Price $210.88 (1Y +43.02%) / Market Cap approx. $266 billion / P/E Ratio approx. 67x (trailing 12 months, GAAP) / P/B Ratio approx. 18x / Dividend Yield — (No dividend)
The market capitalization is calculated by multiplying the approximately 1.2612 billion outstanding shares by the stock price. The trailing P/E ratio of 67x is the figure divided by the earnings per share of $3.17 for the past 12 months under standard accounting (GAAP). The adjusted earnings per share for 2027 projected by analysts is $5.22, and when divided by this, the P/E ratio becomes approximately 40x.
Looking at the chart from the left, after hitting a high in the $160 range at the end of October 2025, the stock fell 8.6% the day after the July-September quarterly earnings in November, and treaded water around $130 during the winter. It sank to $116 on March 30, and from there, it recovered more than 50% in just over three weeks until April 22.
In the May earnings for the January-March quarter, despite raising the outlook, the stock fell 13.6% the next day. This was because investors disliked CEO Ullal's comments that component shortages would continue across the industry and pressure profit margins. Since significantly raising the outlook in the August earnings for the April-June quarter, it has risen almost steadily, hitting a record high in October.
5-Year Volatility +765.68% (+$186.52) / All-time High $216.74 (Closing price on October 9, 2026) / Recent Major Decline $129.82 → $64.37 (January 22, 2025 → April 4, 2025, approx. 50% drop)
Arista was founded in 2004 by Andy Bechtolsheim, a co-founder of Sun Microsystems and known as one of Google's first investors, and others. Jayshree Ullal became CEO in 2008, and the company was listed on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2014. Since then, it has split its shares 4-for-1 in 2021 and 2024.
The stock price has increased about 8.7 times in five years, but the journey has not been smooth. In 2025, the stock price halved in about three months, from its high in January to its low in April. This was a period when anxiety about a potential slowdown in AI capital expenditure spread rapidly, fueled by reports of DeepSeek in China releasing a low-cost AI model and the announcement of US tariffs in April.
Since then, in a year and a half, the stock price has reached 3.3 times its low. Mr. Bechtolsheim remains the largest shareholder with 14.6% of the outstanding shares, and Ms. Ullal serves as both Chair and CEO. Kenneth Duda, one of the founding members, serves as President and CTO, and the faces at the center of the technology have not changed much since the founding period.
The mechanism for earning through switches and EOS
Arista's core product is the Ethernet switch that connects servers within data centers. In AI training and inference, tens to hundreds of thousands of GPUs exchange data without rest, so the speed and stability of the network connecting them determine GPU utilization rates.
The semiconductors at the heart of the products are not made in-house but are mainly purchased from Broadcom. What sets them apart is EOS, a network OS that runs as the same single software across all products. Product assembly is entrusted to contract manufacturers such as Jabil, Sanmina, and Foxconn, with production taking place in Malaysia, Vietnam, Mexico, and other locations.
According to the company's explanation, the breakdown of revenue for 2025 was as follows.
By customer type: 48% from large cloud and AI giants, 32% from general enterprises and financial institutions, and 20% from AI-specialized and other cloud operators.
By product: 65% from core products for data centers and AI, 18% from office networks (campus) and wide-area routing, and 17% from software and services.
There are two customers that account for more than 10% of revenue, and in 2025, they accounted for 26% and 16% of revenue, respectively. 42% from just two companies in total. Although the company does not disclose the names, CEO Ullal mentioned Microsoft and Meta as their oldest partners during the earnings call, and they are believed to be these two companies.
The company had approximately 5,115 employees at the end of 2025. The adjusted operating margin for the April-June quarter was 49.9%, meaning nearly half of the revenue remains as operating profit. I believe that a company that buys semiconductors and puts them in boxes is able to achieve profit margins close to those of a software company because of EOS and its long-standing relationships with customers.
💡 Arista is a company that has earned its success through software and customer relationships without owning its own semiconductors. Because its strengths are clear, it is worth keeping in mind from the start its dependence on two large customers and Broadcom, which are parties it cannot control itself.
Earnings details: Guidance raised three times, gross margin declined
From here, we will look at the earnings for the April-June quarter released on August 4. While revenue growth is strong as the headline suggests, there are figures that should be read with caution when breaking down profit margins and revenue sources step by step.
Revenue up 37.7%, full-year guidance to $12.6 billion
Revenue for the April-June quarter was $3.0357 billion, up 37.7% year-on-year and up 12.1% from the previous quarter. This exceeded the approximately $2.8 billion guidance the company issued in May by more than $230 million. Quarterly revenue exceeded $3 billion for the first time, and CEO Ullal reflected that five years ago in 2021, annual revenue was $2.9 billion.
Product revenue was $2.6052 billion (+38.8%), and service revenue from maintenance and software was $430.5 million (+31.3%). GAAP net income was $1.2129 billion, or $0.95 per share. Adjusted earnings per share, excluding stock-based compensation, was $1.02, a 40% increase from $0.73 in the same period last year.
The revenue guidance for 2026 has been raised as follows.
Analyst meeting in autumn 2025: approximately $10.5 billion
February 2026 (October-December quarter earnings): approximately $11.25 billion (25% increase)
May 2026 (January-March quarter earnings): approximately $11.5 billion
August 2026 (April-June quarter earnings): Approximately $12.6 billion (40% increase)
The guidance for the July-September quarter is approximately $3.3 billion in revenue, with adjusted earnings per share of $1.06 to $1.08. Since revenue for the first half was $5.7447 billion, calculating backward from the full-year $12.6 billion, it implies revenue of approximately $3.55 billion for the October-December quarter. Revenue for the second half is about 1.19 times that of the first half, structured so that it can be achieved even without the significant upside seen in the first half.
CEO Ullal stated during the earnings call that all figures, including AI and campus, are trending upward. Furthermore, the guidance is based on the extent to which components can be secured, and there is room for further upside if supply eases. What determines this company's revenue right now is the supply side rather than demand.
While revenue grew by nearly 40%, the gross margin has declined. The GAAP gross margin for the April-June quarter was 62.9%, down 2.3 percentage points from 65.2% in the same period last year. The company cites the increased proportion of sales to large customers with significant discounts as the primary reason.
Another burden is the rising cost of components such as memory. During the February earnings call, CEO Ullal candidly stated that the memory situation had deteriorated significantly, that they had no choice but to accept almost any price to secure supply, and that the pricing was terrible. Although the gross margin for the April-June quarter rose by 1 percentage point from the previous quarter, 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points of this was a temporary boost from tariff refunds.
The company has maintained its 2026 gross margin guidance at 62-64%. Regarding price increases, the explanation was that since they are currently fulfilling backlogs, the impact will be felt toward the end of the year or next year. Costs rise first, and price increases take effect later—following this sequence, they expect downward pressure on the gross margin for some time.
As for the operating margin, revenue growth outpaced expense growth, and the adjusted guidance for 2026 was raised to 48-49%. However, the long-term model for 2026-2029 presented by the company in the fall of 2025 was a gross margin of 60-64% and an operating margin of 43-45%. Current profit margins are higher than the company's own long-term assumptions.
Deferred revenue up 2.5x in a year and a half
The most difficult figure to interpret in Arista's earnings is deferred revenue (the amount for which payment has been received or billed to customers but has not yet been recognized as revenue). Is Open AI Rack Launch Altering The Investment Case For Arista Networks Stock?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 5:10 AM CDT 6 min read
Arista Networks recently launched an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, including the Etherlink SU-144 architecture, to support high-density AI infrastructure with up to 144 accelerators per rack and liquid-cooled designs tailored for extreme power and thermal demands.
The ESUN-based platforms and Netdi foundation aim to give cloud and AI operators an open, standards-focused alternative to proprietary interconnects, linking Arista's hardware closely to neocloud cost-per-token priorities and multi-vendor AI compute ecosystems.
This development also shapes Arista Networks' broader investment narrative, with a focus on the Etherlink SU-144 AI rack-scale expansion.
Spot opportunities around Arista Networks' AI buildout by scanning a hand-picked set of 55 AI infrastructure stocks.
Arista Networks Investment Narrative Recap
To own Arista Networks, you need to believe high bandwidth AI and cloud networking keeps expanding and that hyperscalers and neocloud platforms keep leaning into open Ethernet fabrics rather than closing into proprietary islands. The Etherlink SU-144 launch fits that thesis operationally by deepening Arista's role inside dense AI racks, but the recent product news does not change the basic story that execution depends on a few very large buyers.
In the near term, the key catalyst is how management frames AI fabrics demand and 2026 guidance on the upcoming earnings call, especially in the context of recent share price volatility. The biggest risk is that AI buildouts or U.S. data center permitting slow while Arista has already locked in multiyear chip and memory commitments, which could leave utilization and gross margin under pressure.
The Etherlink SU-144 scale up architecture is the announcement that matters most here because it goes straight to the core AI catalyst for Arista Networks. By extending Ethernet into tightly coupled accelerator domains of up to 144 XPUs per rack and over 1,000 XPUs across racks, the firm is trying to stay aligned with the way large customers design AI clusters.
That same launch also highlights the execution swing factors. Liquid cooled, 100 kW plus racks, UEC based fabrics, and support for multiple scale up protocols increase Arista's footprint but require heavy up front commitments and integration work. If hyperscalers moderate AI capital spending or shift toward more in house solutions, this expanded ESUN and Etherlink stack could take longer to absorb than current plans assume.
What the Current Arista Networks Consensus Is Pricing In
Analysts are effectively telling you that Arista Networks has to keep growing into its AI and cloud ambitions for current expectations to hold. The consensus setup assumes revenue expands at about 26.6% a year over the next few years, while profit margins stay steady at 38.4%. That combination keeps the story firmly tied to execution rather than margin repair.
On earnings, the group forecast points to US$8.2b of profit by 2029 versus US$4.0b today. That is roughly a doubling of earnings, or a 2x step up from current levels, and it comes with a wide spread of views between the most optimistic and most cautious analysts. For investors tracking the AI buildout, that range underlines how much uncertainty still sits around long range demand for Ethernet based fabrics, including platforms like Etherlink SU-144.
The same playbook underpins the revenue line. Consensus numbers imply roughly US$21.4b of sales in 2029 if Arista Networks delivers on the AI and campus targets embedded in recent guidance. That profile lines up with the assumption of mid 20s top line expansion and a business that keeps its profitability broadly where it is today rather than swinging to a very different margin structure.
Valuation thinking in the analyst reports also leans heavily on those 2029 profit targets. To make the current price targets add up, Arista Networks would need to trade on a P/E of about 47.8x those projected earnings, compared with roughly 62.2x on today's earnings base and around 34.4x for the wider US communications peer group. The message to you is simple: belief in the AI networking path, including Etherlink and ESUN driven racks, is what is doing most of the work in these models.
Arista Networks' narrative projects US$21.4b revenue and US$8.2b earnings by 2029. This requires 26.6% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$4.2b from US$4.0b today.

AI data center spending is splitting networking stocks into clear winners and laggards, and the gap between Ciena, Arista, and Cisco reveals which part of the network hyperscalers are actually racing to build.
Published October 19, 2026, 2:06pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Networking hardware is leading a broad technology rebound, and suppliers of optical links and Ethernet switches for AI data centers are drawing the biggest buying. By Monday afternoon, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN | CIEN Price Prediction) stock was up 4% to $347.48. Meanwhile, Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) stock also climbed 4%, hitting $183.32 and keeping pace with the gain in Ciena shares.
Shares of Ciena and Arista are running well ahead of the wider technology group. The iShares U.S. Technology ETF (NYSEARCA:IYW) is up 1.29%. Large-cap tech is advancing at a similar pace, with the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) also up 1.31%.
A sharp pullback in Ciena and Arista shares over the prior week came before the bounce. Hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure remains the core support for Ciena and Arista. Both companies build the networks that move data between and inside AI data centers.
Supply Limits Keep Ciena’s Backlog Growing
Ciena’s fiscal Q3 2026 results showed adjusted EPS of $2.11 against a $1.73 consensus. The company’s revenue rose 37% year over year (YoY) to $1.67 billion.
Cloud providers did the biggest spending for Ciena, accounting for 53% of revenue on 82% YoY growth. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $6.42 billion and issued a preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook calling for at least 30% revenue growth.
Strong demand also shows in Ciena’s backlog, as the company ended Q3 with $8.5 billion on the books and projects to exit fiscal 2026 with over $10 billion. During the earnings call, executives stated, “The demand is absolutely there.” Supply remains the limit, and management doesn’t projects the market to return to balance before 2028.
Optical Links and AI Switches Ride One Spending Wave
Ciena sells optical networking equipment that links data centers, while Arista and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) sell the switches and routers inside them. Pluggable optics were a standout, with Ciena’s pluggables revenue more than doubling YoY in Q3 as the WaveLogic 6 Nano ramped. Notably, CSCO stock is practically unchanged at $107.06 today, so it’s not keeping pace with CIEN and ANET today.
Arista’s EtherLink switches power Ethernet-based AI fabrics in hyperscale data centers. Management frames the Arista 2.0 strategy around networking. The company sees networking as the “central nervous system” for infrastructure, and EtherLink adoption has spread to a broader roster of cloud, AI and neocloud customers.
Scale-across networks, which connect AI training clusters spread over multiple data centers, are Ciena’s next growth leg. Its RLS HyperRail line system, co-created with hyperscalers, is on track for initial customer adoption by year-end and material revenue through 2027. Co-packaged optics offer another lever, with revenue projects to begin in 2027 and grow into 2028 for Ciena.
Improving operating leverage is showing up in Ciena’s results too, with adjusted gross margin expanding 450 basis points YoY to 46.4%. The company’s chief executive asserted in the earnings release that “AI continues to drive compounding waves of network investment.”
Ciena’s growth carries concentration risk, since two customers made up 41.7% of its Q3 revenue. Its outlook also assumes continued AI infrastructure spending by cloud providers, stable optical component supply and no material change to tariff policy.
Next quarter’s results could show whether Ciena can hit its fiscal Q4 2026 revenue guidance of $1.75 billion under tight component supply. Traders will be tracking whether Ciena and Arista shares keep outpacing the iShares U.S. Technology ETF and the Invesco QQQ Trust.
Long-term supplier agreements running through 2029 could ease Ciena’s bottleneck, though recent moves in its shares show how quickly sentiment can turn. Investors may want to hold smaller share stakes until the supply squeeze resolves.
